- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.1), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience or reversal.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 73+), producing exaggerated highs in 30d forecast; cap or smooth peak predictions.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., +1.4 → -1.1) within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; add lagged correction factor to forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30d horizon, model often misses early downward momentum; if sentiment turns negative after 10–15 days, reduce forecast slope early.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.5), model tends to overfit recent noise; use 18-day moving average as baseline for smoothing.
